title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 7 close: gratuitous affection first; Romans 9:12; Ephesians 1:5
pass_a_gloss: From which you see that not foresight of human cooperation, but the gratuitous affection of God alone is presupposed as antecedent to the election and predestination of singular persons. Which the Apostle illustrated in that most celebrated example of Jacob and Esau, which is set forth in Romans 9:12. And he also expressed it in clear words in Ephesians 1:5. Who predestined us, whom he would adopt as sons through Jesus Christ unto himself, according to the good pleasure of the utterance of his will. And here enough has been done for this argument.
pass_b_english: From this you see: not foresight of human cooperation, but God's gratuitous affection alone is presupposed as antecedent to the election and predestination of particular persons. The Apostle illustrated it in that famous example of Jacob and Esau (Romans 9:12), and said it in plain words in Ephesians 1:5: who predestined us to adoption as sons through Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will. And here enough for this argument.
source_text: Ex quibus videtis, non praescientiam humanae cooperationis, sed gratuitum affectum Dei solummodo praesupponi ut antecedens ad electionem et praedestinationem singularum personarum. Quod Apostolus illustravit in illo celeberrimo exemplo Jacobi et Esavi, quod proponitur Rom. ix. 12. Et etiam disertis verbis expressit Ephes. i. 5. Qui praedestinavit nos, quos adoptaret in filios per Jesum Christum in sese, pro beneplacito affatus voluntatis suae. Atque hic huic argumento factum est satis.
